name: dev-cycle
description: Software delivery with a producer-reviewer loop, a refuter on specifications and decisions as board memory. Change Request work is reviewed only after publication and waits in accepted until its story integrates; inline work without a Change Request is reviewed and finishes directly, or skips review when its review field says none, so the delivery invariants hold (spec section 6.10). For Change Request work the check set handoff gates review and the check set landing gates the story's integration; inline work runs no suite (spec section 6.12). A blocked element records why and where it was blocked, resumes there, and repeated blocks escalate to a person. Loop limits are parameters a project tunes (params), and the rework and rollback loops are unbounded by default, as today. Template of the curator-playbook-dev-cycle package (skills/orchestrator/data/playbook.json).

rework_limit.description: How many requests for changes one element may take before it escalates to the operator. none by default, as today: some work legitimately needs thirty rounds, and delivery loop detection stays the soft signal (spec sections 6.2, 7.3). A project sets it, for example { "rework_limit": 5 }.

rollback_limit.description: How many rollbacks of one element's accepted work (landed rework, invalidation) before it escalates. none by default, as today; the validator warns about the unbounded cycle development -> review -> accepted -> development (spec section 10).

block_limit.description: How many times one element may be blocked before the next block goes to the operator.

reviewer.description: Independence is checked against the provenance of the developer run that produced the revision under review (spec section 9).

refuter.description: Tries to refute a draft against recorded decisions. Records the ledger verdicts with a refutation detail: accepted/no-contradiction, changes_requested/contradiction, stop_the_line/human-decision-needed (spec section 12).

operator.description: The project's people map binds the operators group to roster principals.

task_class.description: Code work goes through a Change Request; metadata and research work is usually inline and takes the route guarded by delivery.cr-absent.

review.description: Review level, written at creation from policy.review.default and set afterwards by the orchestrator or a person, never by the producer: a field the workflow's guards read is authority-bearing (spec section 5.2). none lets inline work finish on the producer's outcome without review; any level may still be reviewed, and work under a Change Request always needs a reviewer's acceptance (invariants 2 and 3).

block_kind.description: Why the element is blocked. Required on every entry into blocked and cleared by the kernel on exit, so a reason is never read for the next block.

blocked_from.description: The state the element was blocked from. The kernel writes it on entry into blocked (record_source) and clears it on exit; the resume routes read it. Only the kernel writes it: no run, session or person does (spec section 6.1).

review.description: none: the outcome closes the research without a review. Set by the orchestrator or a person, never by the researcher (spec section 5.2).

statement.description: Set before the decision leaves proposed.

scope.description: What the decision governs, for example a module, a file or the whole project.

links.description: Specifications, elements and commits it concerns.

decision.description: Board memory the refuter checks drafts against. Its initial state is human-owned, so only a person may supersede an accepted decision (spec section 4.2).

decision-needed.description: Only a person can choose; the choice is recorded as a decision.

transitions.description: The outcome must be recorded after the epic entered hld (evidence freshness, spec section 6.3).

integrating.description: The orchestrator integrates the story as one unit.

transitions.description: The join lists every terminal state of every contained type (dev-task: done, closed; research-task: done, closed; design-task: approved, closed) plus the dev-task's waiting state accepted. The check set landing gates the integration: delivery.integrated is emitted only after it passed on the exact tree or head that lands. A unit with no accepted revision integrates at once.
The delivery module emits integration-failed only with a rollback authorization (invariant 4).

accepted.description: Accepted Change Request revision waiting for its story's integration; the leaf never reaches done before integration.

escalated.description: The rework loop hit its limit, the reviewer stopped the line, or the element kept getting blocked; a person decides.

blocked.description: Work cannot continue. block_kind says why: a dependency on other work, input only a person can give, a missing capability, or a transient failure. The kernel records the state the element came from and clears both fields on exit.

transitions.description: Stricter than invariant 3: work under a Change Request is reviewed only after its revision is published, and only with the check set handoff's evidence for that revision; inline work without one is reviewed directly and runs no suite. Any review level may be reviewed.

Inline work whose review level is none finishes on the producer's outcome; like all inline work it runs no check set, as today. Work under a Change Request cannot take this route (delivery.cr-absent), so it still needs a reviewer's acceptance.
Rework, bounded by the parameter rework_limit, unbounded by default. With a bound of N, the request for changes after the Nth escalates instead.
Inline work without a Change Request finishes on acceptance (invariant 1's inline route).
Emitted for every element of the integration unit when the story lands.

A rollback of the accepted revision (landed rework, invalidation). The loop development -> review -> accepted -> development is bounded here when the project sets rollback_limit: the limit keeps one counter per element for this transition, so the rollback after the Nth goes to the operator instead of back to development. Unbounded by default, as today (v4.3).

Every entry records block_kind (the state requires it), and the kernel records the source state. The limit, block_limit (3 by default), keeps one counter per element for this transition, whichever state it leaves: with the default, the fourth block of one element goes to the operator instead.
A dependency block releases automatically when its last blocker ends, back to the state the element was blocked from.

The orchestrator resumes the element where it was blocked once the cause is gone. A block from open returns to open, so open -> development still applies its estimate and assignee guards. This manual resume and the automatic release above are two transitions (spec section 6.2).
Input only a person can give, or a capability nobody has: the orchestrator hands the element to the operator.

escalated.description: The reviewer stopped the line; a person decides.

transitions.description: Research whose review level is none closes on its outcome.
A reopen from a terminal state: only a human actor, because proposed is human-owned.
